newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends off on profit-taking ahead holiday.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends off on profit-taking ahead holiday.

text.p: Finnish shares fell on Wednesday, bucking an upbeat sentiment on other European bourses, as profit-taking set in after five days of rises, and as bourse locomotive Nokia extended losses, brokers said.
The HEX general index fell 0.96 percent to 3,002.04 -- 1.3 percent below the fresh all-time high 3,041.92 set on Tuesday. Volume was a muted 453 million markka with 20 percent in Nokia.
Trend-setter Nokia traded in the red throughout the session and ended 5.50 markka down at 328.00 in reaction to a sell-off in technology stock on Wall Street on Tuesday.

Merita, Finland's biggest bank, rallied briefly on its higher-than-forecast first-quarter earnings, but closed down 0.20 markka at 17.80. Operators said Merita's profit had been boosted by gains from the disposal of equities.
Merita was hit by profit-taking after recent steep gains in anticipation of the earnings report, traders said.
Forest industry shares were soft following a 1.5 percent decline in U.S. paper stocks overnight, and on profit-taking after recent sharp gains. The clearly weaker dollar also hurt.
UPM-Kymmene, Europe's biggest forestry group, closed 0.50 markka lower at 122.00 markka.
The Helsinki bourse will be closed on Thursday for the Ascension day public and market holiday.
